observations: Photo 0 shows a black DSLR camera body with 'Nikon' on the top plate and 'D750' on the front right side. The camera is placed on a brown cardboard box labeled 'Nikon' and 'D750'.
Photo 1 shows the same camera from the rear, with the LCD screen and control buttons visible. The same box is underneath.
The camera appears to be in good physical condition with no visible cracks or dents.
The box is plain brown cardboard with a yellow Nikon logo and large 'D750' text printed on it.
The background suggests a retail or second-hand electronics store with other boxes and glass display cases.
No lens is attached to the camera; the lens cap is on the body.

claims.claim: The camera is a Nikon D750.
claims.evidence: The model name 'D750' is clearly visible on the camera body in photo 0 and photo 1, and on the box.

claims.claim: The camera is in working condition.
claims.evidence: No video or functional test is shown. The screen is off and no operation is demonstrated.

claims.claim: The camera is being sold as a body only.
claims.evidence: No lens is attached, and the lens cap is on the body in both photos.

risks.risk: The camera may be non-functional or have internal damage.
risks.proof: A video showing the camera powering on, menu navigation, and shutter operation.

risks.risk: The camera may have a damaged sensor or lens mount.
risks.proof: A close-up photo of the sensor (with the mirror up) or the lens mount interior.
risks.if_unproven: priced as having potential sensor or mount damage

risks.risk: The camera may be stolen or have a compromised serial number.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the serial number on the camera body, preferably from the bottom plate.
risks.if_unproven: priced with risk of legal or warranty issues

proof_requests: Video of the camera powering on and operating the shutter and menu.
Close-up photo of the sensor and lens mount.
Clear photo of the serial number on the bottom of the camera body.
response.reason: The camera is clearly identified as a Nikon D750, but functional and physical condition risks remain unproven. Without proof of operation and internal condition, it cannot be priced accurately.
